title: 5 British schoolgirls, 14-15, build firebreak robot, represent UK globally
content:
Five schoolgirls from Kent, aged between 14 and 15, have built a robot with five-metre folding arms to help fight wildfires. Their work has earned them the chance to represent Great Britain at an international robotics competition in South Korea. The team from The Folkestone School for Girls, known as Team Meglabyte, designed the robot to clear dry plants and create paths that remove fuel from the spread of fires. The school's robotics club was only founded in 2024, but it has now been chosen to represent Great Britain at the FIRST Global Challenge in Incheon.
Designing a solution to growing wildfire risks
The international competition brings together student teams from more than 190 countries to work on major environmental and technology problems. This year's challenge focuses on preventing, controlling and recovering from wildfires in a warming world. For the competition, the Folkestone students designed an autonomous vehicle with long, folding arms that can clear paths up to five metres wide through dry vegetation. The system removes plants and other surface material that can fuel a fire, creating natural firebreaks that can slow the spread of flames without putting firefighters directly in danger.
According to a statement on the official website of The Folkestone School for Girls, the students have been working to improve the robot before the global competition: "The Folkestone School for Girls robotics team, Team Meglabyte, are thrilled to be representing Great Britain at the First Global Challenge in South Korea."
Working with local firefighters
The five students worked with professional firefighters to make sure their design could deal with the real conditions faced during wildfires. According to a report by Kent news outlet Shepway Vox, the students spoke with Kent Fire and Rescue Service during the early stages of the project. The firefighters helped them understand how wildfires spread across difficult terrain. Their advice led the team to focus on building a lightweight and stable robot that could extend its arms across uneven ground without tipping over. The students also used standard parts supplied by the competition organisers to program the robot's autonomous driving system. The software allows the machine to avoid obstacles, clear debris and work on its own in areas where thick smoke could make remote control difficult.
National selection and fundraising
The team's success comes only two years after the school's robotics program was created. Despite having less experience than some international teams, the Kent students won the national selection process and secured Great Britain's single place in the competition. To help pay for their trip to Incheon and the materials needed to build their robot, the team launched a public crowdfunding campaign. On their official Crowdfunder page, the students explained their goal of representing Britain and encouraging more girls to study science and technology: "Our aim is to inspire young girls across GB into STEM and globally raise awareness about this year's competition theme of wildfires. Each year a single robotics team from a school in Great Britain is sent to compete in a robotics competition on the global stage. This year, five girls from the all-girls state school Folkestone School for Girls have been selected to represent the nation in South Korea to compete with their robot. The girls need your help to get them to the competition!" The students are also using the opportunity to create outreach programs for primary schools. These projects will give younger pupils basic coding kits and lesson plans showing how engineering can be used to solve real environmental problems. The FIRST Global Challenge will take place in Incheon, South Korea, where the five Folkestone students will put their robot to the test against teams from countries around the world.

title: À Molenbaix, l’art contemporain s’invite dans les rues et les champs et attire des visiteurs de toute la Wallonie
content:
À Molenbaix, l'art contemporain s'invite dans les rues et les champs et attire des visiteurs de toute la Wallonie
Il reste deux semaines pour découvrir "Butor", la première biennale d'art contemporain en campagne. Dix-neuf artistes, entre champs et hameaux.
- Publié le 19-09-2026 à 12h01
Le centre du village et le hameau de Butor voient passer de nombreux visiteurs, depuis quelques semaines. Ils viennent de différents coins de Wallonie, mais aussi des Flandres et de France.
"Butor" et douceur
Marcher de la ferme d'Ecavée au centre du village permet de découvrir un sentier singulier, en céramique gravée de mots. "De Molenbeek à Molenbaix", "Ce chemin est celui de tous" ... Citadins et ruraux se souviennent de venelles, sentes, petites voies, ruelles, chemins de pavés et de liens. Les enfants apprécient particulièrement cette oeuvre de Various Artists, un collectif également auteur d'un totem et de quelques interventions insolites.
"C'est ma petite-fille !" annonce fièrement Christian Collie quand des visiteurs s'approchent du terrain de foot. Léa - en miroir - est peinte par Charlotte Beaudry sur bois chantourné, aux couleurs du club. La jeune footballeuse de quinze ans joue à présent à Avelgem, elle est de plus, vu son talent, reprise dans la sélection nationale des Jeunes à Mons. Son grand-père, qui évolua au Racing de Tournai, fait partie du comité de foot de Molenbaix.
Un pas plus loin, Raphaël De Coster a créé une "zone de rupture potentielle", en utilisant un cordeau. Ligne droites et penchées, tendues vers la cime d'une structure qui puise son énergie dans un geste géométrique résolu. Chemin du centre, Lise Duclaux a placé des affiches porteuses de slogans courts, limpides : "Nous ne sommes que les autres". L'église Saint-Ghislain abrite des recherches picturales de Charlotte Beaudry, un autel à sainte Rita (Jacques Charlier) et une étonnante sculpture de Maaerten Vanden Eynde : un tronc d'arbre scié, posé sur une ancienne balance en fonte. L'oeuvre interroge l'équilibre, la fragilité, la pesanteur.
Lieux et liens
"C'est un choc, ce jaillissement !", s'exclame Frédérique, venue de Lasne à la rencontre de l'exposition. Devant "La terre saigne", fontaine de Laurence Dervaux, elle évoque son réflexe de "juguler la plaie", "voir arriver une ambulance" "une énorme puissance suggestive" . "Des visiteurs parlent ici autant de vie que de mort, songeant aux guerres comme aux souffrances infligées à la planète", souligne Caroline, l'une des guides de l'exposition.
Des groupes et duos se croisent, échangeant leurs impressions à propos du parcours, de la campagne, des nombreuses haltes proposées. Aucun artiste n'est oublié dans les conversations, les précisions et questions. Les interventions en extérieur comme en intérieur ouvrent des perspectives, déclenchent la surprise, l'admiration, la réflexion collective. Et cette certitude d'être au coeur d'une approche que l'on dit contemporaine : l'intégration au paysage, à la nature, l'assurance d'une discrétion privilégiée, la présence du symbole et de la beauté.
"Butor", au départ de la ferme d'Ecavée à Molenbaix, du jeudi au dimanche, de 10h30 à 18h. Possibilité de visites guidées. Jusqu'au 4 octobre.

title: [한경에세이] 콩이가, 준우가, 옥분 씨가 행복한 추석
content:
AI 추천 뉴스




[한경에세이] 콩이가, 준우가, 옥분 씨가 행복한 추석
김미경 서울 은평구청장




우리 집에 선물처럼 새로운 가족이 찾아온 지도 어느덧 두 해가 흘렀다. 이름은 콩이, 풀네임은 ‘김콩’. 하얀 얼굴에 복슬복슬한 털, 까만 눈 두 개와 까만 코 하나. 처음 데려왔을 때 부모님께서 “콩만하게 작네!”라며 지어준 이름이다. 아침마다 내 방문을 긁으며 “앙!”하고 나를 깨우고, 매일 부모님과 함께 불광천을 산책하며 일상에 녹아든 녀석을 보면, 엄연히 콩이가 우리 집의 막내아들 같은 강아지라는 사실을 실감한다.
콩이와 함께 살면서 가족에 대해 새삼 생각하게 된다. 돌이켜보면 우리가 가족이라고 부르는 모습은 과거와 많이 달라졌다. 피로 맺어진 혈연만이 가족의 전부는 아니다. 말없이 곁을 지키는 반려동물도, 홀로 살아가지만 자신의 일상을 단단하게 꾸려가는 청년과 어르신도 우리 사회의 소중한 가족이다.
명절만 되면 마음 한구석이 묵직해지는 소식을 접한다. 연휴 기간이면 유기동물이 급증한다는 뉴스다. 또 따라붙는 이야기가 있다. 온 가족이 모이는 명절일수록 오히려 고립감을 느끼며 쓸쓸함을 견뎌야 하는 이웃의 이야기다. 구청장으로 현장을 누비다 보면 그런 이야기를 듣는다. “혼자 사는데 아플 때 돌봐줄 사람이 없어 걱정이에요.”, “홀로 계신 어르신이 외로움을 많이 타세요.”, “우리 강아지가 아플 때 마음 편히 맡길 곳이 있으면 좋겠어요.”
나는 행정이 살펴야 할 가족의 범위를 조금씩 넓혔다. 지난 2020년 서울시 최초로 ‘반려동물도 가족’이라는 개념을 행정에 도입해 전담 팀을 꾸렸다. 청년부터 중년, 어르신에 이르기까지 1인 가구와 자립준비청년이 혼자서 모든 어려움을 감당하지 않도록 돌봄 안전망도 촘촘히 살피고 있다. 행정이 해야 할 일은 누군가의 외로움이 혼자 감당해야 할 몫이 되지 않도록 곁을 내주는 것인지도 모른다.
실제로 나는 추석이 되면 이들의 삶터를 찾아간다. 어릴 때 엄마와 함께 장보기가 소원이었다는 자립준비청년과 시장에서 장을 보고, 전통과자를 만들어 관내 아동복지시설에 나누고, 대조동 청년주택의 공유주방에서 1인 가구 청년들과 명절 음식을 준비한다. 그럴 때면 행정이란 결국 하나의 삶을 들여다보는 일이라는 생각이 든다. “동생들과 함께 나누고 싶었어요”라고 수줍게 건넨 자립준비청년의 이 한마디 속에서 가족의 의미를 되새긴다. 따뜻한 음식을 함께 나누고 서로의 안부를 묻는 사람이 바로 식구이자 가족이 아닐까.
민족 대명절 추석이다. 이번 연휴만큼은 형태가 어떠하든 우리 주변의 그 누구도 소외되지 않았으면 좋겠다. 홀로 명절상을 차리며 쓸쓸해할지 모를 우리 동네 준우와 옥분 씨의 안부를 한 번 더 돌아보고 싶다. 사람뿐만 아니라 이웃집의 해피와 까미, 우리 집 막내 콩이까지, 저마다의 자리에서 따뜻한 한가위를 보내길 바란다. 우리 옆의 가족들을 들여다보고, 좀 더 마음을 쓰는 추석 말이다.

title: Mural of rapper Macklemore painted in Gaza after Ed Sheeran tour furore
content:
Mural of rapper Macklemore painted in Gaza after Ed Sheeran tour furore
- Artists in Gaza painted a mural of rapper Macklemore wrapped in a Palestinian flag to thank him for supporting Palestine after he was removed from Ed Sheeran's tour.
- Macklemore donated US$1 million from the tour to Gaza aid groups, sparking matching pledges from other celebrities and highlighting the need for sustained support.
- Gaza remains devastated with stalled reconstruction and ongoing humanitarian needs, as locals value celebrity solidarity for raising awareness and pushing for peace.
AI generated
GAZA/JERUSALEM – Artists in Gaza have painted a mural of Macklemore wrapped in a Palestinian flag on a huge slab of concrete in the ruins of Gaza City, after the US rapper was kicked off Ed Sheeran’s upcoming tour for calling for a “Free Palestine”.
The mural, on a slab that leans against ruined buildings surrounded by rubble, depicts the “Thrift Shop” rapper raising a fist in the air.
“Thank you for using your voice for Palestine,” it reads.
“We wanted to send a message to thank rapper Macklemore in this simple way,” said Anne Redwan, 26, who designed and painted the mural with fellow artist Qusai al-Helo.
“As an artist living under siege here in Gaza, we are waiting for support from anyone who can see (the) persecution we live under,” she said. “We can paint murals bigger than this to express our feelings.”
Macklemore, who has long supported Palestinian causes, was cut from British pop star Sheeran’s musical line-up over remarks on stage criticising Israel’s military assault in Gaza, which was launched after Hamas-led fighters attacked Israel in October 2023.
Sheeran said he was unable to keep Macklemore on the tour after stadium owners refused to let him appear. US billionaire Robert Kraft, owner of Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts where his New England Patriots American football team plays, said he had barred Macklemore from appearing there for anti-Semitism, which the rapper denies.
Nearly a year after a ceasefire ended major fighting in Gaza, reconstruction has yet to begin. Most buildings have been destroyed and more than two million residents are confined to around a third of the enclave’s territory, mostly in tents or crowded rooms in damaged buildings among the ruins.
A US-brokered plan to end the war has stalled, with negotiators failing to agree to conditions for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops.
The furore over Sheeran’s tour has led to a series of pledges from those involved to send money. Macklemore said on Sept 16 he would donate his US$1 million (S$1.3 million) in net earnings from the tour to six aid groups supporting Gaza.
Kraft, in turn, said Sheeran had told him he would donate US$2 million for aid in the region and had asked him to match the pledge. Sheeran has not commented on any donations. Macklemore’s donation drew a matching US$1 million pledge from Ms Rachel, a popular children’s TV personality.
Aid agency officials said the boost in celebrity attention could help bring more support to Gaza, where nearly all residents rely on aid for food, water, medical care and shelter.
“But what’s really most important is that people who have been so generous keep fighting over a sustained time,” said Toby Fricker, a local official with UNICEF. “That’s why we really call for sustained support, not one-off peaks, but sustained.”
Hussein Murtaja, who runs a Gaza humanitarian group that provides mental health support to children, said Macklemore’s solidarity matters more than the money he donated.
“When artistes of this stature, with this many followers or fans, all come to know more about the cause, and support reaching a political solution, support achieving peace for the people of Gaza... That means a great deal to us.” REUTERS

title: El alcohol está de capa caída y en Euskadi no creen que sea impedimento para divertirse: llegan las barras "light" a Bizkaia
content: Hace más de un año ya apuntábamos a una gran crisis del alcohol entre los jóvenes. Más allá de la presión social, esa vieja aliada, el bebercio tradicional está disminuyendo entre las generaciones actuales. Bajo este contexto, Bizkaia acaba de estrenar un híbrido: la discoteca de siempre, con su barra habitual, y al lado, otra barra a 0,0 grados. Mismo precio, misma pista, cero alcohol. La idea llega meses después de que abriera en Hernani la primera discoteca silenciosa de Euskadi, con 200 auriculares y tres canales de música por colores. Dos experimentos y un mismo cliente de fondo: alguien que ya no bebe, o bebe bastante menos, que hace quince años. Menos borracheras. Según la última Encuesta sobre Uso de Drogas en Enseñanzas Secundarias, el 51,8% de los adolescentes españoles ha bebido en el último mes, la cifra más baja desde 1998. Las chicas beben más que los chicos, por cierto. O eso dicen las estadísticas. Lo que está claro es que las borracheras han caído al 17,2% y el consumo en atracón, al 24,7%: ambos, mínimos históricos. En Euskadi la tendencia se repite: los datos del Gobierno Vasco confirman que el descenso es más notable entre los menores de 34 años, tanto chicos como chicas. Salir, beber, el rollo de siempre. Aquí llega el dato dañino: quien más bebe de forma arriesgada no es la juventud, sino la gente de 35 a 54 años, con un 32% en niveles de riesgo, frente al 17% de los menores de 35. En Bilbao, vecinos de Abando e Indautxu llevan tiempo señalando a los “cuarentones” como el colectivo más conflictivo del ocio nocturno, por encima de los jóvenes que ocupan las salas los fines de semana. El txikiteo pierde parroquia. La tradición vasca de ir haciendo chiquitos (tomar chatos o vasos pequeños de vino) de bar en bar resiste, pero con menos público. Según la Asociación de Hostelería de Bizkaia, la población joven se ha reducido prácticamente a la mitad respecto a hace quince años. Una “sangría” que golpea directamente la facturación nocturna. El ocio se desplaza hacia el tardeo, que representa el 26% de la facturación en hostelería nacional, y el botellón, inexistente antes de los 2000, que se lleva una parte importante del gasto que antes iba para discotecas. Es cancerígeno, punto. Un recordatorio, porque la ciencia no deja mucho margen para el matiz aquí. La Agencia Internacional para la Investigación del Cáncer, brazo de la OMS, clasifica el alcohol como carcinógeno del grupo 1 desde 1988: la misma categoría que el tabaco, el amianto o la radiación. Está vinculado a al menos siete tipos de cáncer (boca, faringe, laringe, esófago, hígado, colon-recto y mama) y provoca, según la propia IARC, el 4% de todos los cánceres diagnosticados en el mundo, más de 740.000 casos y 401.000 muertes al año. El mecanismo es conocido: el etanol se transforma en acetaldehído, un cancerígeno en sí mismo, y además genera inflamación y estrés oxidativo. La OMS recuerda que no existe un nivel de consumo seguro. Esa copa de vino diaria que durante años se vendió como cardiosaludable es mercadotecnia. En Xataka Madrid se ha llenado de "fiestas de dopamina": se acabó el alcohol, llegan las ensaladas y los baños de hielo Bailar en silencio. El otro empujón viene de la ley. España restringe la música en muchos locales a partir de las diez de la noche, y algunos bares vascos han resuelto el problema cambiando altavoces por cascos inalámbricos: la fiesta sigue, pero desde la calle no se oye nada. El bar de Hernani que lo estrenó reconoce que la medida, pensada solo para cumplir la normativa, acabó siendo su mejor reclamo comercial. Demasiado ruido. title: Newsom signs California law forcing insurers to pay for toxic smoke cleanup after Los Angeles fires
content:
Even after the January 2025 Palisades and Eaton fires were out, many Los Angeles County residents with homes still standing were not in the clear.
California has adopted what LAist described as a first-of-its-kind statewide policy: Gov. Gavin Newsom signed two bills requiring insurers to pay for smoke testing, contamination cleanup, and temporary housing while a home cannot yet be safely reoccupied.
Here's what to know
Assembly Bills 1642 and 1795 lay out more specific duties for insurers when smoke damage claims are filed.
Since the fires, owners of houses that remained standing have filed 13,000 smoke damage claims, according to the state Department of Insurance.
The bills say insurance companies must evaluate homes for smoke-related contamination, cover remediation when necessary, and keep paying temporary living costs until a home is cleared as safe again.
The California Department of Toxic Substances Control must finish standards for lead and asbestos testing and cleanup by the end of 2028. Rules for heavy metals and other pollutants are due by the end of 2029.
In a news release, Newsom said, "These new protections will make insurer obligations clearer and give homeowners more financial flexibility when they need it most."
More background
Officials said the smoke from the Los Angeles County fires was especially dangerous because the destruction happened in urban areas.
As buildings burned, they released contaminants like lead paint and asbestos. The fires also consumed cars, appliances, and other manufactured items.
Families may face contamination even if their homes never caught fire.
For some residents, that has meant prolonged uncertainty, fights with insurers and the added expense of staying in hotels or rentals while they wait to learn whether returning home is safe.
A group called Eaton Fire Residents United found lead, asbestos and heavy metals lingering in homes even after professional remediation companies had cleaned them. According to LAist, the group's executive director is Jane Lawton Potelle.
What's being done?
The new laws are designed to shift more of the financial responsibility for smoke-related cleanup and displacement onto insurers rather than residents.
By creating statewide testing and remediation standards, California is aiming to reduce the need for homeowners to battle insurers one claim at a time over whether cleanup is justified.
Supporters of the bills say science-based standards could make the claims process less confusing and more consistent. Assemblymember John Harabedian, who authored one of the measures, described the issue as one of evidence instead of insurer judgment.
LAist reported that insurance industry groups objected to giving the Department of Toxic Substances Control this rulemaking role instead of the California Department of Insurance.
As Harabedian said, "Science, not an insurance company's opinions, will determine whether a home is safe."
Where can I learn more?
In fire-prone states, smoke hazards, insurance pressures, and policy fights are changing what recovery looks like after major wildfires. The stories below explore how contamination standards, coverage rules, and public health concerns keep surfacing long after the flames are out.
• After the Los Angeles fires, parents feared toxic smoke began harming children before birth.
• In California, State Farm's retreat showed every company matters in wildfire-prone insurance markets.
• In Sacramento, lawmakers clashed over overhaul California's wildfire response as residents pressed for change.
• In Colorado, a new law changed how homeowner risk is calculated for insurers.
Many Los Angeles-area families still face a steep gap between their insurance payout and the true cost of rebuilding.

title: Zimtschnecken und Co. - Worldskills: Steirerin bäckt gegen 22 Nationen an
content:
Zwölf junge Steirer kämpfen als Teil des 48 Köpfe starken, rot-weiß-roten Teams aktuell in Shanghai um die Medaillen der Berufsweltmeisterschaften Worldskills. Am ersten Tag herrschte Kampfgeist – und es flossen Tränen.
In der Halle 4.1 des National Exhibition and Convention Center riecht es süß nach Plundergebäck und nicht nach Veranstaltungszentrum. Jennifer Lueger knetet, mehlt den Teig und rollt ihn aus. Schnellen Schrittes schiebt sie das Gebäck ins Rohr, die Kappe verdeckt ihr Gesicht. So will die 21-Jährige sich voll und ganz auf den Wettkampf fokussieren.
„Sie ist sehr konzentriert“, sagt ihre Mutter Manuela, die durch die Plexiglaswand zuschaut. #teamjenny steht auf den Ärmeln der T-Shirts, die Papa Jakob, Schwester Lara und Schwager Markus aus St. Jakob im Walde extra anfertigen haben lassen, um Jennifer in Shanghai zu unterstützen. „Ich habe eigentlich ein bisschen Flugangst“, sagt Jakob Lueger. „Aber jetzt, wo ich hier bin, würde ich es echt bereuen, zu Hause geblieben zu sein.“
„Bei den Broten ist sie super“
Normalerweise steht die 21-Jährige in der Backstube in Miesenbach bei Birkfeld. 8500 Kilometer Luftlinie entfernt bäckt sie gegen 22 Nationen an, von Kasachstan bis Mexiko, auf einer Fläche, die 20-mal so groß ist wie die Grazer Messe. Nach den Zimtschnecken mit Apfelchutney am Mittwochvormittag war die Anspannung zur Mittagspause groß, erzählt Mama Manuela, die Jennifer einen Burger vorbeibrachte. Es flossen ein paar Tränen. „Bei den Broten ist sie super. Die sind perfekt geworden.“
Bei den Bäckern herrscht Schichtbetrieb, deswegen wird Jennifer Lueger schon am Donnerstag fertig und kann dann ihre Teamkameraden anfeuern. Etwa Logistiker Paul Zadravec aus Leitring. Er sitzt insgesamt vier Tage lang mit dicken Kopfhörern vor dem Computer, mit Oreo-Keksen und Cola am Tisch, und löst Probleme mit Lieferketten, telefoniert mit Firmen, nimmt Aufträge an.
Medaillenvergabe am Sonntag
Zwölf Steirer sind insgesamt beim Wettbewerb dabei, Österreich stellt das größte Team aus Europa und hat traditionell in den Handwerksberufen gute Chancen. 2024 in Lyon ging eine Goldene an Fliesenleger Florian Gruber aus Aigen im Ennstal. Am Sonntagabend wird feststehen, wer die heiß begehrten Medaillen mit nach Hause nehmen kann.
Ob Edelmetall oder nicht: „Als Mama ist man auch bei Rückschlägen da“, sagt Manuela Lueger. Sie und Papa Jakob sind schon jetzt „gewaltig stolz“ auf ihre Tochter.

title: Partnership is key to ending AIDS – UK leadership can get us there faster
content:
Partnership is key to ending AIDS – UK leadership can get us there faster
Ending AIDS as a public health threat is still possible by 2030, writes Courtenay Howe. But we need a renewed commitment to all the things that have helped create the progress we have made over the last few decades
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
It’s not about one country having all the answers and another having all the questions,” Kirsty McNeill, the minister for international development and Africa, said this week, describing the UK’s approach to partnerships, “but instead, bringing together different strengths to achieve far more than either of us could alone.”
Many of us who work in international development and advocacy will resonate with this framing. Shifting from hierarchical forms of aid to a system based on solidarity and partnership is something that many of us have tirelessly advocated for, and has long been a driving principal of the global HIV response.
Community involvement and leadership have been central to the response and the resulting progress speaks for itself. In 2002, the year the UK co-founded the Global Fund partnership, only 102,000 people had access to HIV treatment, less than 1 per cent of people living with HIV.
New data from the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria released this week shows that last year 26.9 million people, in countries where the Global Fund invests, had access to antiretroviral therapy for HIV. The number of AIDS-related deaths in 2025 was 57 per cent lower than in 2010, from 1.3 million to 570,000.
But the current environment in which communities and organisations such as the Global Fund advance efforts towards ending AIDS as a public health threat cannot be overlooked.
In 2025, donor government funding for HIV decreased by $2.1 billion (£1.6bn) compared to 2024, representing a 25 per cent cut. Funding cuts globally have had a significant impact particularly on HIV prevention efforts and women are disproportionately affected. In sub-Saharan Africa women account for 6 out of 10 new acquisitions and adolescent girls and young women (aged 15-24 years) remain at high risk with 3000 new HIV acquisitions per week in 2025.
The UK’s own funding cuts, reducing the ODA budget to 0.3 per cent last year, raises concerns about a step back from international political and financial leadership in global health. The welcome shift in international development towards a new collaborative and solidaristic model still requires the UK’s important commitment to advocating for and supporting partnership and community leadership on the global stage.
The communities that had been at the forefront of the HIV response have been impacted hardest by these funding cuts. For many community-led organisations, their delivery of critical HIV prevention and provision of support to people living with HIV has reduced by 50 per cent. Alongside devastating funding cuts, we also see a rollback on human rights and the criminalisation of marginalised communities increasing for the first time since UNAIDS began tracking these trends.
Ending AIDS as a public health threat is still possible by 2030. But we need a renewed commitment to community leadership and human rights. We need scale-up and rollout of innovations such as the twice-yearly jab for HIV prevention, lenacapavir, and continued partnership to support more sustainable and self-reliant country responses to the HIV response.
We need scientific and medical advances to be accessible to low- and middle-income countries. Over the next few years, UK political leadership and sustainable funding will be critical in determining whether we stay on track to meet this goal.
Courtenay Howe is head of advocacy at STOPAIDS

title: Referendum gegen neue AKWs in der Schweiz kommt laut Bündnis zustande
content:
Damit dürfte die Stimmbevölkerung an der Urne über die AKW-Frage befinden können.
Der «Tagesanzeiger» berichtete zuerst über den Sammelstand. Das Bündnis «Nein zu neuen AKW» bestätigte diesen am Samstag in einem Communiqué. Die AKW-Gegnerschaft hätte noch fast drei Wochen Zeit gehabt, um die für ein Referendum nötigen 50'000 Unterschriften zu sammeln.
Hinter dem Referendum stehen die SP, die Grünen, die GLP, Teile der Mitte-Partei sowie zahlreiche Organisationen wie die Schweizerische Energie-Stiftung und Greenpeace Schweiz. Sie bekämpfen den vom Parlament denkbar knapp verabschiedeten Gegenvorschlag zur Volksinitiative «Jederzeit Strom für alle (Blackout stoppen)».
Dieses Begehren haben die Initianten inzwischen bedingt zurückgezogen. Der Gegenvorschlag erfülle das Kernanliegen der Initiative - die Aufhebung des Kernkraftwerk-Verbots - bereits, hiess es.
Das Bündnis «Nein zu neuen AKW» wiederum wirft dem Bundesrat und dem Parlament vor, am Willen der Bevölkerung vorbei zu politisieren. Die Stimmberechtigten hätten sich im Rahmen von vergangenen Abstimmungen klar für eine auf erneuerbaren Energien basierende Zukunft ausgesprochen, hiess es in ihrer Mitteilung.
Die Beteiligten planen, die Unterschriften am 6. Oktober bei der Bundeskanzlei einzureichen. Kommt das Referendum offiziell zustande, dürften die Schweizer Stimmberechtigten frühestens am 28. Februar 2027 über die Gesetzesänderung abstimmen können.

title: Rice bran—source for antimicrobial, biodegradable food packaging film
content:
Rice bran is a plentiful agricultural byproduct that is often underused, but research from the Arkansas Agricultural Experiment Station shows it could be a source of biodegradable food packaging with built-in antibacterial properties.
Antimicrobial resistance is a significant global health threat. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, more than 2.8 million antimicrobial-resistant infections occur each year in the United States alone.
For the past year, with funding support from the Arkansas Biosciences Institute, a multidisciplinary team of scientists led by Mahfuzur Rahman has explored how plasma technology could contribute to new antimicrobial strategies.
The team is using plasma, a state of matter visible in natural phenomena such as the Northern Lights, to improve the value-added capabilities of rice bran and rice bran protein.
Rahman is an assistant professor in the Department of Food Science for the experiment station, the research arm of the U of A Division of Agriculture, and the Dale Bumpers College of Agricultural, Food and Life Sciences at the U of A.
The research showed that treating a clear film made from rice bran protein with argon-generated cold plasma inhibited foodborne bacterial pathogens, including E. coli, Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a bacterium known for its antibiotic resistance.
The plasma treatment inhibits bacterial growth in two ways: It creates microscopic spikes on the film and triggers a chemical reaction that produces and releases hydrogen peroxide, a strong oxidizing agent with antimicrobial properties.
After exposure to the plasma-treated rice bran films, bacterial populations of all pathogens declined within eight hours and were inhibited from regrowing 24 hours after application. Conversely, untreated rice bran films showed marked bacterial growth, the study showed.
Rahman said the research demonstrates that argon cold plasma offers a green, novel approach for transforming rice-processing byproducts into sustainable, functional materials.
"This idea actually came from the microchip industry," Rahman said. "They use the plasma for what's called etching to assemble semiconductor layers, and we transferred that idea to the rice bran films."
For the study, researchers compared films made solely from rice bran with films made from rice bran protein. The rice bran protein film appeared to react more favorably, with more microscopic spikes, or etches, and higher hydrogen peroxide concentrations. In the rice bran protein films, the plasma increased surface roughness 3.3-fold, compared with 1.06-fold in films using solely rice bran.
While cold plasma was known to improve physical and chemical properties in synthetic polymer films, Rahman said its antibacterial effects in rice bran-based biopolymer films had not been previously reported.
The team also examined how the treatment affected the films' physical properties, such as water vapor transmission rate, tensile strength and thermal stability. The antibacterial effect, the study noted, likely resulted from the "combined influence of retained reactive species, enhanced wettability, increased surface roughness and changes in surface chemistry."
A manuscript of the study has been submitted for peer review to a scientific journal, with plans to submit a proposal for further studies on a potential medical application.
"I am very thankful to ABI for supporting the study to explore the untapped potential of rice bran in food packaging and the medical industries," Rahman said.
Advancing antimicrobial films
In addition to its biodegradable and antibacterial qualities, Rahman said the research on plasma-treated rice bran film will help further develop effective antimicrobial films, which is "one of the most important challenges in modern materials science."
Conventional antimicrobial films, he added, often incorporate additives such as nanoparticles and antibiotics to inhibit microbial growth, raising health concerns because these additives can migrate from the packaging material into food and potentially enter the human body.

title: A lifetime of service: Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid's contributions to security and defence
content: Dubai: The career of the late Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid Al Maktoum was closely linked to key milestones in the history of military and security work in Dubai. Throughout his career, he assumed leadership responsibilities in the military and security sectors and witnessed the development of the emirate's institutions and the modernisation of their capabilities.The late Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid received his military education at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst in the United Kingdom before returning to Dubai and joining the Central Military Region base.He rose through the ranks until he assumed command of the base. During his leadership, the base underwent significant development, strengthening its position as one of the leading military facilities supporting the UAE's national defence system.A significant milestone in his security careerThe year 1997 marked a major milestone in his security career. On 24 December 1997, the late Sheikh Maktoum bin Rashid Al Maktoum, then Ruler of Dubai, issued Decree No. 14 of 1997 appointing Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum as Deputy Chief of Police and Public Security in Dubai.The decree not only appointed him to the position but also authorised him to exercise the powers of the Chief of Police and Public Security in the latter's absence, placing him among the emirate's senior security leadership.Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid assumed this responsibility at a time when Dubai was experiencing rapid urban, economic and population growth. These transformations brought increasing security demands and required the continuous development of policing capabilities, human resources and institutional structures.During his years in office, Dubai Police underwent successive stages of development and modernisation in parallel with the emirate's transformation and the expansion of its economic, tourism and commercial sectors.Security remained one of the key pillars supporting this growth, whether through the protection of lives and property or by providing the safe environment necessary for society and the economy to thrive, as policing became increasingly specialised and professional.Promotion to the rank of Lieutenant GeneralHis career took another significant turn in April 2005 when His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, then Crown Prince of Dubai, Minister of Defence and Chief of Police and Public Security, issued a decree promoting Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid from Major General to Lieutenant General.The promotion came after several years of service as Deputy Chief of Police and Public Security.This period witnessed further expansion and modernisation within Dubai Police. Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid continued to hold the rank of Lieutenant General, and his name remained closely associated with Dubai's police and public security system.As a senior leader within the force, he witnessed an important era in the development and modernisation of the security apparatus. His years of service remain part of the institution's history and were linked to major transformations that helped shape modern Dubai.CondolencesSecurity and national leaders mourned Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, recalling his long record of service, his contributions to strengthening security and stability in Dubai, and the impact he left through the positions he held.A lifetime of serviceLieutenant General Dhahi Khalfan Tamim, Deputy Chief of Police and Public Security in Dubai, said: "With hearts that believe in God's will and decree, and in acceptance of His judgment, we bid farewell to a towering national figure and a symbol of sincere national service, the late Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, whose passing marks the end of a distinguished chapter filled with dedication and devotion to serving the nation across many important stages and fields."He added: "The late Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid was an outstanding figure who combined military discipline, strategic vision and sports leadership. He was raised on love of the homeland and the values of leadership and chivalry. After graduating from the prestigious Royal Military Academy Sandhurst, he assumed responsibility within the Central Region military command in Dubai and later led it with efficiency and competence, becoming a model of loyalty and military professionalism."Dhahi Khalfan said the late Sheikh Ahmed's contributions extended beyond the military field to include the security, economic and sporting sectors."I was honoured to work alongside him and always knew him to be sincere and deeply committed to the security, stability and progress of Dubai. In his role as Deputy Chief of Dubai Police and Public Security, he left a clear and lasting impact on the development of security work."He added: "In sport, he had a strong leadership presence, particularly through his presidency of Al Wasl Club, where he contributed significantly to the club's progress and sporting stature, in addition to the economic and social roles he undertook throughout his successful career."Concluding his tribute, he said: "As we remember the virtues of the departed and his lasting national achievements, we mourn the loss of a loyal brother, a dedicated leader and a companion who devoted his life to serving Dubai and the United Arab Emirates."A prominent national figureLieutenant General Abdullah Khalifa Al Marri, Commander-in-Chief of Dubai Police, extended his sincere condolences to His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum and the Al Maktoum family.He said the UAE and Dubai had lost a prominent national figure who contributed to strengthening the armed forces and left a lasting legacy of dedication and service.Al Marri said Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid embodied the values of loyalty, belonging and commitment to elevating Dubai's standing, contributing to the service of the nation through the various responsibilities he held.He highlighted the late Sheikh Ahmed's important role in supporting security and stability, particularly during his tenure as Deputy Chief of Police and Public Security in Dubai, when he contributed to the development of the security establishment and its capabilities.Al Marri added that Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid represented a model of sincere national service, combining official responsibilities with social and humanitarian contributions while supporting Dubai's comprehensive development across the security, economic and humanitarian sectors.He concluded by saying that Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid's contributions would remain a source of appreciation and pride, and prayed for was one of Dubai's loyal sons.He said the late Sheikh Ahmed left a lasting imprint on security work through his role as Deputy Chief of Police and Public Security and his dedication to strengthening security, safety and the protection of Dubai's achievements.Al Matroushi noted that Sheikh Ahmed worked alongside his brothers and his father, the late Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum, during an foundations of securityKhalifa Ibrahim Al Seles, Chief Executive Officer of the Security Industry Regulatory Agency, said the UAE had lost one of its most loyal sons.He said Sheikh Ahmed bin Rashid title: Minister calls MBG focus on disadvantaged regions as priority
content:
Indonesia's Ministry of Villages and Development of Disadvantaged Regions has urged the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) to prioritize the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program for residents in frontier, underdeveloped, and outermost (3T) areas.
Director General for the Acceleration of Disadvantaged Regions Development Samsul Widodo said the ministry had been communicating with BGN to direct the flagship program toward regions with the greatest needs.
"We are now drafting a letter from the Minister to the BGN chief to emphasize the importance of prioritizing disadvantaged regions," he said during the "Strategy for Accelerating the MBG Program in 3T Regions" forum, which was monitored online from Jakarta on Wednesday.
He noted that 30 districts across Indonesia remain classified as disadvantaged regions, stressing that they warrant special attention in the implementation of the nutrition program.
As an example, Widodo pointed to the insufficient number of MBG kitchens in Central Sumba District, East Nusa Tenggara Province, and several other regions.
Against that backdrop, he reiterated the urgency of expanding the MBG program while taking into account the specific conditions and needs of underserved communities.
BGN earlier announced that it had removed 1,653 educational institutions from the list of MBG recipients, redirecting resources to communities with greater needs, including those in 3T regions.
The BGN Chief, Sudaryono, said the delisted institutions comprised international schools and elite private schools.
He noted that the schools did not rely on operational assistance funds offered by the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education.
Meanwhile, Coordinating Minister for Food Affairs Zulkifli Hasan said the government is prioritizing the activation of 111 MBG kitchens across 3T regions in nine provinces, including six Papuan provinces.

title: Rus preživio napad medvjeda: "Bila je tišina. Onda sam osjetio da je netko iza mene"
content:
Rus preživio napad medvjedice. "Slomila mi je ruku na 10 mjesta, otkinula čeljust"
VIKTOR Seligejev ostao je s teškim ozljedama lica, s više od deset prijeloma ruke i polomljenim rebrima nakon napada medvjedice u ruskoj tajgi. Unatoč svemu, uspio je ustati i, teško ranjen, prijeći oko kilometar i pol do prijatelja.
RIA Novosti razgovarala je s njim u sklopu priče o ljudima koji su preživjeli napade medvjeda. Seligejev kaže da mu je medvjedica potpuno otkinula gornju čeljust, smrskala nos i teško ozlijedila lice.
"Liječnici koji su me prevozili šaptali su međusobno da me s takvim ozljedama nema smisla voziti u bolnicu. Ali imao sam sreće", rekao je.
Medvjedica ga napala s nekoliko metara
Tog dana otišao je u tajgu skupljati cedrove šišarke. Navikao je hodati šumom sam, pa su njegovi prijatelji krenuli u jednom smjeru, a on u drugom.
"Bila je tišina i potpuni mir. Odjednom sam osjetio da je netko iza mene. Okrenuo sam se, a na otprilike tri metra od mene bila je medvjedica", ispričao je za RIA Novosti.
Kaže da je i ranije nailazio na medvjede i znao da ne smije pobjeći. Pokušao se zakloniti iza stabla, ali medvjedica ga je dohvatila.
"Malo me vukla po čistini i onda se bacila na mene. U meni je sve počelo krckati, rebra su se lomila. Onda me počela gristi", rekao je.
Prema njegovoj procjeni, životinja je težila oko 200 kilograma.
Više od deset prijeloma ruke
"Na kraju mi je potpuno izgrizla ruku. Imao sam više od deset prijeloma. Skinula mi je kožu s lica, smrskala nos i potpuno otkinula gornju čeljust", ispričao je.
Kaže da su mu liječnici poslije rekli da je imao sreće što mu medvjedica nije probila lubanju. Na glavi su mu ostali brojni tragovi ugriza, a na licu i danas ima duboke ožiljke.
Napad je, prema njegovim riječima, trajao nekoliko minuta, a zatim se medvjedica udaljila.
"Možda je mislila da sam mrtav. Ili su je dozvali mladunci", rekao je.
Teško ranjen prešao kilometar i pol
Kad se uvjerio da se životinja udaljila, Seligejev je ustao i krenuo prema prijateljima.
"Bili su oko kilometar i pol dalje. Teturajući sam hodao i vikao. Ni sam ne znam kako sam to uspijevao s čeljusti koja mi je visjela. Došao sam do ceste i srušio se. Ali prijatelji su me čuli", prisjetio se.
Iako teško ranjen, uspio im je objasniti kako da mu pruže prvu pomoć.
Nakon što su mu previli rane, jedan od prijatelja krenuo je oko 20 kilometara do mjesta na kojem je bilo signala kako bi pozvao pomoć. Ostali su od grana napravili nosila, prenijeli ga do kampa i dali mu sredstvo protiv bolova.
Sedam sati čekanja na helikopter
Helikopter su čekali oko sedam sati. Seligejev kaže da je cijelo vrijeme bio pri svijesti.
Predvečer se počeo snažno tresti od hladnoće zbog velikog gubitka krvi.
"Izgubio sam više od dvije litre krvi. Dečki su grijali vodu i oko mene stavljali boce kako bi me zagrijali", rekao je.
Helikopterom je prevezen u Republičku kliničku bolnicu u Abakanu. Ondje su mu liječnici operirali teško ozlijeđenu ruku i počeli rekonstruirati lice.
Oporavak nakon sedam operacija
Dosad je prošao sedam operacija, a čekaju ga dodatni zahvati. Od napada se oporavlja već petu godinu.
Unatoč svemu, kaže da i dalje odlazi u tajgu i da se medvjeda ne boji. Dodaje da ove godine primjećuje posebno mnogo medvjeda.
Ipak, neke je navike promijenio.
"Naučio sam lekciju. Nabavio sam psa. On će me sigurno upozoriti ako se predator približi", rekao je.

title: Christian Bale's California foster care village was in the works for nearly 20 years. It's now open
content:
Image courtesy of Jesse Grant, accessed via Getty Images
Claim:
Actor Christian Bale helped build 12 homes in a $22 million village in Palmdale, California, that aims to keep siblings in the foster-care system together.
In September 2026, a heartwarming claim (archived) circulated online that "Batman" actor Christian Bale helped build 12 homes in a $22 million village in Palmdale, California, that aimed to keep siblings in the foster care system together.
For example, one Threads post about the alleged project was captioned:
I absolutely LOVE this. Christian Bale spent roughly 17 years fighting to make this happen. This week, his foster-care village opened in Palmdale, California: 12 homes built specifically to help keep siblings together when they enter foster care.
The claim was true. Bale and Together California, a charity founded by the actor; his wife, Sibi; and UCLA Dr. Eric Esrailian, broke ground on the project in 2024, and Bale cut the ribbon on the homes on Sept. 9, 2026.According to Together California, the village, located near Palmdale, features 12 homes and a community center. It was expected to start welcoming children from October 2026. The project was estimated to cost $22 million at the time of the groundbreaking, according to internationalmedia.
Bale told (archived) The Associated Press at the ribbon-cutting that the project had been underway for almost 20 years and that he was originally inspired to take part by his daughter. Bale said:
Just looking at my little girl, she was 3 at the time, she's 21 now, took that long to get this together, but to know, imagine if she got taken and then on top of that getting split from siblings, know, absolutely shameful.
CBS News reported in 2025 that "trained foster parents" would take care of the children living in the village.
According to AC Martin, the architects on the project, Together California's "Village for Brothers and Sisters" would feature 12 townhouse units for children in foster care, two studio units for young adults transitioning out of the foster system, a 7,000-square-foot community building and outdoor space.

title: East Bank Berbice Logging Association to be reconstructed, concessions to be expanded
content:
The government is moving to strengthen the operations of small loggers and firewood cutters on the East Bank of Berbice, with plans to reorganise their association, expand its forestry concession and create new opportunities for economic activity.
Minister of Natural Resources Vickram Bharrat made the announcement during a meeting with loggers and residents of Mara on Friday, following a commitment he made during a recent engagement with loggers at the Guyana Forestry Commission’s New Amsterdam station.
Minister Bharrat said the meeting identified several challenges affecting the sector, with many centred on the functioning of the existing association and the need for greater cooperation among its members.
“We have agreed on a number of ways forward in which we’re going to address some of the challenges and issues. However, most of the challenges that exist among them revolve basically around the functioning of the association and members of the association working together,” the minister said.
He noted that the association had reportedly not renewed its concession for the past two years, while concerns were also raised regarding the distribution of taxes collected by the association and the absence of regular meetings and elections.
As an immediate step, the Guyana Forestry Commission will meet with the firewood association and the other small associations operating on the East Bank of Berbice on September 27 in Mara to facilitate the formation of a new East Bank association and the election of an executive team.
“After that is done, we made a commitment that we can extend the concession that they presently hold,” Minister Bharrat explained.
The existing association currently holds approximately 8,500 acres, with the government proposing an additional 5,000 acres to accommodate the growth in membership and allow more persons to benefit from the concession.
Beyond forestry, the minister has also proposed that the association explore opportunities in the mining sector.
He said consideration will be given to working with the association towards a medium-scale mining block, allowing interested members to pursue mining alongside their logging activities.
The government is also seeking to expand the economic opportunities available to residents through skills training and value-added production.
Minister Bharrat announced plans for the establishment of a full-fledged furniture-making facility on the East Bank of Berbice, with training to be provided by the Guyana Forestry Commission.
Residents will be trained to produce items including school furniture, wardrobes, cabinets and kitchen cupboards, creating opportunities for employment and entrepreneurship.
Additionally, a jewellery-making course is expected to be brought to Berbice before the end of the year, which will be provided free of cost, is intended to equip interested persons with skills in jewellery making and provide pathways towards becoming registered entrepreneurs or securing employment with established jewellery businesses.
The minister said the initiatives form part of efforts to broaden the economic benefits available to communities whose livelihoods are traditionally centred on farming and forestry.
“I’m very pleased with the outcome. I’m very pleased with the momentum that we had today and the feedback as well from residents and loggers,” he said.
The initiatives are expected to provide residents with opportunities to move beyond the sale of raw timber and diversify their income through furniture production, mining and jewellery-making.

title: '딸바보' 아빠, 여직원에 우호적…통계로 확인

'딸바보' 아빠, 여직원에 우호적…통계로 확인
딸이 첫째면 女직원 비중 4.5%↑
"비슷한 실력이면 여성 채용"
"비슷한 실력이면 여성 채용"
첫 번째 자녀로 딸을 얻은 남성 관리자가 여성 직원에게 더 우호적이라는 연구가 발표됐다. 딸을 키우며 달라진 여성에 대한 인식이 여성 직원 채용과 승진 결정에도 영향을 미친다는 분석이다.
니나 스미스 덴마크 오르후스대 경제학과 교수 등이 글로벌 경제 학술지 ‘경제학연구리뷰’에 기고한 연구에 따르면 남성 관리자의 첫째 자녀가 딸일 경우 해당 기업에서 여성 직원이 차지하는 비중은 전체 평균 대비 4.5% 높았다. 남성 직원의 소득 평균 대비 여성 직원의 소득 비율도 4.1% 상승했다. 이런 변화는 딸이 태어난 직후부터 나타나 해당 관리자가 회사를 떠날 때까지 이어졌다.
첫째가 아들이거나 둘째 이후 딸이 태어났을 때는 뚜렷한 변화가 나타나지 않았다. 첫째가 딸일 때 남녀 간 임금 격차가 줄어든 것은 새 직원을 뽑거나 승진자를 정할 때 여성을 선택하는 사례가 늘어난 결과로 나타났다. 기존 여성 직원의 임금을 올려주거나 해고를 줄이는 모습은 관찰되지 않았다.
연구진은 1992~2017년 덴마크 기업의 고용 동향과 기업 행정자료를 분석했다. 연구진은 경영 의사결정권자의 영향을 명확히 하기 위해 한 명의 관리자가 운영하는 소규모 기업을 조사 대상으로 삼았다. 조사 대상 기업은 덴마크 전체 기업의 90% 이상을 차지했다.
여성 채용이 늘었다고 해서 남성보다 자격이 떨어지는 지원자를 선택한 것은 아니었다. 새로 채용된 여성의 경력과 자격은 딸을 낳지 않은 관리자가 운영하는 기업에 채용된 남성과 비슷한 수준이었다. 비슷한 조건의 남녀 지원자를 놓고 첫째 딸을 얻은 남성 관리자가 여성을 선택하는 경향이 강해졌다는 의미다. 회사에서 가장 많은 임금을 받는 직원이 여성일 확률도 2%포인트 높아졌다.
여성 채용 확대에도 기업 실적은 유지됐다. 매출과 전체 고용 규모, 근로자 1인당 부가가치 등 주요 경영지표에서 유의미한 변화가 나타나지 않았다.

title: South African circus gives young performers a new route forward
content:
Circus
Clutching an aerial hoop on a Johannesburg circus stage, a young performer pauses for a split second before launching into the air and gliding, drawing cheers from the crowd below.
For 29-year-old Brian Ngobese, who grew up in South Africa’s impoverished Alexandra township, moments like this mean more than applause. The circus has given him a stage, a livelihood and a way to turn his talent into work.
“We just want to show people that we can make it out of the township,” said Ngobese. “What you want to accomplish, you can actually make it.”
Behind the colorful spectacle is a social program that helps performers from under-resourced communities turn talent into opportunity and paid work.
Alexandra is one of Johannesburg’s most densely populated townships, marked by high poverty and unemployment despite being just a few kilometers from Sandton, a major financial district dubbed the “richest square mile in Africa.”
For many young South Africans, missing out on training opportunities often means spending years on the fringes of the labor market.
Many tend to stay unemployed rather than move into informal work, according to the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development.
Unemployment among 18 to 34-year-old South Africans was about 45% in 2025, according to Statistics South Africa.
Performers train for years to build the strength, flexibility and discipline needed to work professionally. Some become instructors, while others take paid work with production companies or The Cirk, a professional Johannesburg circus company.
The program is designed to sustain itself through training, performances and other circus work rather than relying entirely on outside funding.
Ngobese’s older brother first introduced him to South African street and social dancing. He later moved into contemporary, hip-hop and other styles, building on a love of performing that began in childhood.
He found circus almost by accident after auditioning as a dancer for a Joburg Theatre production in 2019. What began as a short job became a career when The Cirk invited him to stay and train.
Ngobese received support for training and transportation through Jozi Circus School’s youth development program. The school partners with The Cirk, where he now works.
“Cirk was like an adventure,” he recalled. “When I saw people flying, I was like, ‘Is this what they’re doing here?’ Okay, this is life. I’m like, ‘Let’s go for it.’”
Years later, Ngobese would quickly mend a tear in his costume, his eyes streaked with red and yellow makeup, as he prepared to go on stage.
The animal-free circus show blends choreography with gravity-defying acrobatics on silks and hoops. Ngobese plays a “little star” journeying through oceans, fantastical lands, and fiery fortresses in search of what will make him shine.
The role reflects Ngobese’s own journey into a world he had never imagined for himself.
Circus also brought Ngobese together with Zenzele Letsoela, a fellow dancer from Alexandra.
“I’m grateful to Cirk for bringing me another brother I didn’t know I actually needed in my life,” said Ngobese.
Together, they combined dance with circus skills and began attracting attention beyond the school. “People were like, ’Where are those guys? We want those guys. We want to see more,” he said.
Letsoela, 38, trained in ballet and pantsula, a fast-paced South African township dance style. Moving into aerial acrobatics brought an unexpected challenge: he is terrified of heights.
“I wouldn’t say I’ve learned to overcome my fear of heights, but I’ve learned to work around it,” he said.
Hoisted about two meters above the stage as a magical tree, Letsoela stays in character despite the nerves.
“People don’t see that I’m actually nervous going into the air. I look very comfortable,” he said. “And I’m like, if only you guys knew, I am dying inside.”
By the end of the show, Ngobese, glittering in gold as the little star who has finally found where he belongs, was back in the air — hanging from an aerial silk by one arm as gasps gave way to more cheers.

title: Krakau: Mittagessen unter polnischen Arbeitern
content: Ich sitze in einer Milchbar, auf polnisch bar mleczny, in Krakau und versuche, so zu tun, als wäre dies ein spontaner, authentischer Moment meines Lebens und nicht das Ergebnis von 47 geöffneten Tabs mit „Geheimtipps, alternativ, Krakau“ in der Suchleiste. Ich habe mir nämlich vorgenommen, die Dinge wirklich zu erleben. Deshalb sitze ich jetzt zwischen Menschen, die einfach nur mittagessen.Die Milchbar, ein polnisches Paralleluniversum aus sozialistischer Kantine und kulinarischer Zeitkapsel, riecht nach Suppe, Frittierfett und Vergangenheit. Sie ist eine Institution aus den 1960er- und 1970er-Jahren, als die kommunistische Regierung kommunale Essensplätze subventionierte, um Arbeitern warme Mahlzeiten zu ermöglichen. Die Einrichtung ist funktional – ein Wort, das hier bedeutet: Alles stammt aus einer Zeit, in der Design noch kein Gefühl war. Ich beobachte an der Theke, wie Plastiktabletts über Linoleum rutschen, das mehr Geschichte gesehen hat als ich. Ich bestelle etwas, das ich nicht aussprechen kann, und nicke dabei überzeugt, um meine Unsicherheit zu überspielen. Die Frau hinter der Theke nickt nicht zurück. Ich falle für sie in die Kategorie „Touristin, leicht überfordert, aber bemüht“. Danach suche ich mir in der Ecke einen leeren Plastikstuhl an einem Tisch aus demselben Material.Zu den aktuellen Folgen des KURIER Reise Podcasts „Stadt.Land.Meer.“Am Tisch neben mir sitzt ein Mann, der seine Suppe isst, als wäre sie eine ernsthafte Aufgabe. Sein Kollege kommt zurück, trägt abgenutzte Arbeitskleidung, in der der Bauschutt noch im Stoff hängt. In seinen Händen balanciert er zwei vollgepackte Teller mit Kotlet schabowy (Schweinsschnitzel), und Placki ziemniaczane (Kartoffelpuffern). Während ich den Tisch neben mir beobachte, wird meine Bestellung am Tresen abgestellt: Pierogi ruskie, Kotlet schabowy und Kartoffeln. Es sieht aus wie eine Entscheidung, die jemand anderes für mich getroffen hat – was der Wahrheit entspricht. Ohne die Hilfe der Kassiererin hätte ich mich für etwas anderes entschieden. Und da sitze ich, in einer polnischen Milchbar, und versuche, Bedeutung aus gekochten Kartoffeln zu ziehen.Vielleicht ist dies kein Ort für große Gedanken. Vielleicht ist es einfach ein Raum, in dem die Menschen essen, weil sie hungrig sind. Die Atmosphäre hat mich längst umschlossen, und auch ich möchte nur noch essen.Es schmeckt ehrlich.Als ich gehe, klebt mein Tablett ein wenig. Draußen ist Krakau wieder hübsch, als hätte es mich nie in seine Küchen gelassen.

title: Today in history: Haiti military coup leaders agree to Aristide’s return
content:
Overview:
On Sept. 18, 1994, Haiti’s military leadership, led by Gen. Raoul Cédras, agreed to relinquish power and allow the return of democratically elected President Jean-Bertrand Aristide after a final diplomatic mission led by former U.S. President Jimmy Carter, then-Sen. Sam Nunn and retired Gen. Colin Powell. The agreement came as a U.S.-led military operation was already underway.
On Sept. 18, 1994, Haiti’s military leaders agreed to relinquish power and allow the return of democratically elected President Jean-Bertrand Aristide, averting a forced United States military intervention scheduled for the following day.
The agreement came three years after a military coup overthrew Aristide on Sept. 30, 1991, and after years of international efforts to restore Haiti’s constitutional government.
Former U.S. President Jimmy Carter led the final diplomatic push, along with then-Sen. Sam Nunn of Georgia and retired Gen. Colin Powell, who had served as chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The three traveled to Haiti on Sept. 17 at President Bill Clinton’s request, who authorized the mission while keeping the U.S. military operation on schedule.
A last-minute diplomatic mission
The Carter-Nunn-Powell delegation arrived in Haiti with little time to reach an agreement. The Clinton administration had secured U.N. authorization for the use of force to restore Haiti’s elected government and had prepared an invasion force of nearly 25,000 military personnel under Operation Uphold Democracy. The operation was scheduled to begin Sept. 19.
Through his Carter Center, the late President Carter had been involved in Haiti well before the 1994 crisis. He supported Haiti’s electoral process in 1987 and helped monitor the December 1990 election, in which Aristide was elected. After the 1991 coup, the center continued working with international efforts to restore constitutional government.
Carter, Nunn and Powell met with Gen. Raoul Cédras and other Haitian officials as negotiations continued through the night of Sept. 17 and into Sept. 18.
The talks nearly collapsed after Haitian military officials learned that U.S. troops were already moving toward Haiti. Carter later recalled that Brig. Gen. Philippe Biamby accused the delegation of using the negotiations to distract Haiti’s military leadership while U.S. forces prepared to enter the country.
The delegation eventually met with Haiti’s provisional president, Émile Jonassaint. According to Carter’s account, he made a final appeal to Jonassaint, who responded that Haiti would choose peace.
Jonassaint and Cédras then signed an agreement under which the military leadership would leave power and Aristide would return as president by Oct. 15.
The agreement did not cancel the U.S. operation. Instead, it changed how the operation would unfold. U.S. troops entered Haiti beginning Sept. 19 as part of a peaceful transition rather than through a forced-entry invasion. The U.S. military worked with Haitian forces to facilitate the transfer of power.
Aristide returned to Haiti on Oct. 15, 1994 — three years after he had been overthrown. The U.S.-led operation eventually transitioned to a U.N. mission, and Haiti held presidential elections in 1995.
The Sept. 18 agreement became a pivotal moment in Haiti’s post-coup history and in Haiti-U.S. relations, demonstrating how negotiations conducted under the pressure of imminent military action produced a peaceful transfer of power rather than a forced invasion.

title: A cell death screen identifies macrophage-depleting agents with therapeutic potential
content: Macrophages are critical regulators of inflammation and tissue homeostasis, yet aberrant macrophage activation contributes to a wide spectrum of inflammatory and malignant diseases. Therapeutic strategies that directly reduce macrophage numbers have shown promise, but macrophage survival pathways remain incompletely defined, limiting the development of targeted therapeutic strategies. Here, we establish a high-throughput screening platform to identify small molecule inhibitors that impair macrophage survival. Screening a library of more than 2,000 targeted compounds in a cell survival assay, combined with in silico and in vitro analysis of macrophage specificity, revealed the identification of three potent inhibitors: BIX-01294, GSK-J4, and Masitinib. All three compounds downregulated leukemia inhibitory factor receptor (LIFR), whose inhibition markedly reduced macrophage viability. In vivo, these inhibitors effectively depleted large peritoneal macrophages, ameliorated key symptoms of macrophage activation syndrome (MAS), and suppressed tumor growth in a syngeneic transplanted melanoma model as well as in an autochthonous lung cancer model. Together, these findings identify small molecule-mediated macrophage depletion as a promising therapeutic strategy and establish an experimental approach to uncover regulators of macrophage survival.

title: How to get digital copies of your UAE government documents on your smartphone for free
content: Dubai: If you’re a Dubai resident, you know that paperless transactions and communications are the way to go. That’s why the emirate has made getting digital copies of all official documents a simple process.Here’s how you can get digital versions of all your government-issued documents, right from your smartphone.Why do I need digital copies of documents?The shift to digital document management, rather than reliance on physical hard copies, is inevitable in a visionary city like Dubai.The government of Dubai has been taking proactive steps to create a fully paperless government for years. Launched in 2018, the Dubai Paperless Strategy eliminated more than 336 million sheets of paper used for government transactions every year, saving time, resources and the environment.Digital Dubai, the government entity that’s tasked with digitalising all aspects of life in Dubai, is leading the emirate’s shift toward a fully integrated, smart government.In April this year, His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, directed all government entities in the emirate to integrate services for individuals and businesses into a unified digital ecosystem within one year, with Digital Dubai overseeing its implementation.As part of these initiatives, ensuring government-issued documents are available to all residents without the need for paper, is a key aspect of the city’s vision. What kind of documents can I request, as digital copies?According to Digital Dubai, your UAE PASS permits you access to a host of documents available in official digital formats. Here are just a few examples of documents you can own digitally:Emirates IDPassport for UAE citizensDriving licenceVehicle registration card (Mulkiya)Attested academic certificates and recordsPeople of determination card (Sanad)How do I request digital copies? You will require your UAE PASS, which is your national digital identity, to request a digital copy of a government-issued document. Follow these steps to make your request:Download the UAE PASS app through the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Log in with your biometric information.At the bottom of the home screen, tap on ‘Documents’ in the menu bar. Tap on ‘Request a document’.You will now be able to view a list of all official documents that can be requested, such as driver’s licence or academic qualifications equivalency certificate. Find your required document and click ‘Request’.Your Emirates ID card information will be used to request the document. Select ‘Confirm request’. Wait for the process to complete.Once the process is complete, you will receive a notification via the app. Click on ‘View document’. You will be to see the digital version on your app.Click on the three dots beside the document to be able to view more details and access other facilities, such as saving the document as a PDF, seeing the date issued, and removing the document. Fee: The service is free of charge.

title: Campanha promove rastreios ao cancro da cabeça e pescoço
content:
Hospitais promovem, na próxima semana, rastreios ao cancro da cabeça e pescoço, no âmbito de uma campanha europeia que apela ao diagnóstico precoce da doença, diagnosticada em fase avançada em cerca de 60% dos casos.
Promovida pela European Head and Neck Society (EHNS) e coordenada em Portugal pelo Grupo de Estudos de Cancro da Cabeça e Pescoço (GECCP), a Semana Europeia Make Sense decorre entre 21 e 26 de setembro e reforça este ano a importância do acesso aos cuidados adequados em cada etapa do percurso do doente.
Os promotores da campanha salientam em comunicado que o diagnóstico precoce continua a ser o principal aliado no combate ao cancro da cabeça e pescoço, sublinhando que “a sobrevivência a cinco anos pode atingir 83% no estádio I, mas desce para 28% no estádio IV”.
Quando a doença é identificada numa fase inicial, as probabilidades de cura podem atingir os 90%. No entanto, cerca de 60% dos doentes continuam a ser diagnosticados em fases avançadas (estádios III e IV), o que, afirmam, “tem um impacto significativo no prognóstico, no tratamento e na qualidade de vida”.
“Apesar dos avanços registados no diagnóstico e tratamento, continuamos a assistir a um número demasiado elevado de doentes diagnosticados em fases avançadas. Precisamos de atuar em diferentes momentos do percurso”, afirma Cláudia Vieira, médica oncologista e presidente do GECCP.
A oncologista defende ser necessário aumentar o conhecimento sobre os sinais de alerta, promover a procura atempada de cuidados e assegurar uma referenciação adequada: “Garantir os cuidados certos no momento certo pode fazer a diferença nos resultados e na qualidade de vida dos doentes”.
Entre as principais iniciativas da campanha estão os rastreios para o diagnóstico precoce do cancro da cabeça e pescoço, dirigidos à população em geral.
No Hospital CUF Tejo, em Lisboa, serão realizados rastreios entre 21 e 25 de setembro. No IPO do Porto, a iniciativa está marcada para 22 de setembro, entre as 09h30 e as 13h30, e no IPO de Lisboa, no dia 28 de setembro, entre as 08h30 e as 13h00.
O programa inclui ainda ações de sensibilização, formação e iniciativas dirigidas a profissionais de saúde.
A edição deste ano conta também com o testemunho do ator Rui Santos, que dá a cara pela campanha depois de ter vivido um diagnóstico de cancro na língua.
Em Portugal, são diagnosticados todos os anos entre 2.500 e 3.000 novos casos de cancro da cabeça e pescoço, que pode afetar a cavidade oral, faringe, laringe, cavidade nasal e seios paranasais, comprometendo funções como a fala, respiração, deglutição e alimentação.
Entre os principais fatores de risco estão o tabaco, o consumo excessivo de álcool e a infeção pelo vírus do papiloma humano (HPV).
Os sinais de alerta incluem úlceras na boca que não cicatrizam, rouquidão persistente, dor de garganta, dificuldade ou dor ao engolir, alterações da voz, nódulos no pescoço e obstrução nasal unilateral.
Segundo o GECCP, quando estes sintomas persistem durante mais de três semanas, deve ser procurada avaliação médica.

title: 코로나19 이후 추락한 美 학생들 문해력 회복세
content:
코로나 이후 정체된 美 학생 읽기 성적 회복세
팬데믹 학업 격차 3분의 1 만회 성과
'읽기의 과학' 파닉스 교육 확산이 배경

코로나 이후 정체된 美 학생 읽기 성적 회복세
팬데믹 학업 격차 3분의 1 만회 성과
'읽기의 과학' 파닉스 교육 확산이 배경
구글 검색에서 연합뉴스 기사를 우선적으로 보여줍니다.
(서울=연합뉴스) 신재우 기자 = 코로나19 팬데믹 이후 장기간 정체됐던 미국 학생들의 읽기 성취도가 최근 회복세를 보인 것으로 나타났다.
20일(현지시간) 미국 정치전문매체 더힐에 따르면 교육연구기관 NWEA가 유치원생부터 한국의 중학교 2학년에 해당하는 8학년 학생들의 읽기 성적을 분석한 결과, 지난해부터 올해 사이 성적이 개선되면서 팬데믹 이후 벌어진 학업 격차의 약 3분의 1을 회복한 것으로 나타났다.
NWEA의 메건 쿠펠드 성장모형·분석 담당 국장은 팬데믹 이후 4년간 읽기 성적이 사실상 정체돼 있었던 만큼 이번 개선은 의미가 크다고 평가했다.
전문가들은 최근 성적 개선의 배경으로 각 주가 도입한 읽기 교육 접근법인 '읽기의 과학'(science of reading)을 꼽고 있다.
팬데믹 이후 미국의 약 절반에 해당하는 주(州)가 학교 읽기 교육을 '읽기의 과학'에 맞추도록 법률을 제정하거나 관련 교육 기준을 도입했다.
'읽기의 과학'은 학생들이 글자와 소리의 관계를 체계적으로 익히도록 하는 파닉스 교육에 중점을 두는 교육 방식이다.
개별 글자가 어떤 소리를 내는지, 여러 글자가 결합했을 때 발음이 어떻게 달라지는지를 가르쳐 처음 보는 단어도 스스로 소리 내 읽을 수 있도록 하는 접근이다. 이 방법은 어휘력과 문장의 의미를 파악하는 독해 교육도 중시한다.
이는 미국 학교들에서 그동안 널리 활용돼온 '균형적 문해교육'(balanced literacy)과는 다소 차이가 있다.
균형적 문해교육은 학생들이 모르는 단어를 만났을 때 글자의 개별 소리를 하나씩 익히기보다는 문맥이나 그림 등 여러 '단서'(cue)를 활용해 단어의 의미를 추론하도록 하는 방식이다.
다만 미국 학생들의 읽기 성취도 회복세가 계속될지는 불확실하다.
미국 학생들의 읽기 성적은 1990년대부터 2013년까지 꾸준히 개선됐지만 이후 상승세가 꺾였다. 한 교육 보고서는 이런 학습 정체가 소셜미디어가 확산한 시기와 맞물려 나타났다고 지적했다.

title: Cách thay đổi thói quen để cai thuốc lá
content:
Cách thay đổi thói quen để cai thuốc lá
Hạn chế rượu bia, tránh khói thuốc và thay đổi cách giải tỏa căng thẳng giúp giảm nguy cơ tái hút thuốc.
Hạn chế rượu bia
Theo Very Well Health, uống rượu bia có thể làm giảm khả năng kiểm soát hành vi, khiến người cai thuốc lá dễ hút thuốc trở lại. Nguy cơ này rõ ở người từng có thói quen vừa uống rượu bia vừa hút thuốc. Khi tham gia các bữa tiệc, bạn có thể chọn đồ uống không cồn, ngồi ở khu vực không có người hút thuốc để giảm cảm giác thèm nicotine.
Tránh đến nơi có khói thuốc lá
Khói thuốc và hình ảnh người khác hút thuốc có thể khiến người cai nhớ lại thói quen cũ. Nên hạn chế đến những nơi thường có nhiều người hút thuốc, nhất là trong thời gian đầu.
Tại nhà, nên dọn bỏ thuốc lá, bật lửa, gạt tàn và các vật dụng liên quan. Giữ không gian sống không khói thuốc giúp giảm những tác nhân dễ dẫn đến hút thuốc trở lại.
Thay đổi cách giải tỏa căng thẳng
Nhiều người hình thành thói quen hút thuốc mỗi khi áp lực, mệt mỏi hoặc bực bội. Đi bộ, vận động nhẹ, tắm nước ấm, nghe nhạc hoặc trò chuyện với người thân có thể trở thành những lựa chọn thay thế. Khi cơn thèm hút thuốc xuất hiện do căng thẳng, bạn có thể trì hoãn vài phút, uống nước, nhai kẹo cao su không đường hoặc chuyển sang một hoạt động khác cho đến khi cảm giác muốn hút giảm xuống, theo Times of India.
Xây dựng nếp sinh hoạt khoa học
Thiếu ngủ, bỏ bữa hoặc sinh hoạt thất thường có thể khiến cơ thể mệt mỏi, dễ cáu gắt và khó kiểm soát cơn thèm thuốc. Người cai thuốc lá nên ngủ đủ, ăn đúng bữa và duy trì vận động. Lịch sinh hoạt ổn định giúp hạn chế những lúc buồn chán, căng thẳng dễ dẫn đến hút thuốc.
Người cai nên xác định mục tiêu và kiên trì với quyết định của mình. Thèm thuốc, bứt rứt, khó chịu là những triệu chứng thường gặp và thường giảm dần. Nếu lỡ hút lại, không nên bỏ cuộc mà cần xác định nguyên nhân, rút kinh nghiệm và tiếp tục cai thuốc lá.
Người thân nên kiên nhẫn, tránh trách móc hoặc tạo thêm áp lực khi người cai cáu gắt, bứt rứt hay mất tập trung. Một cuộc trò chuyện hoặc lời hỏi thăm đúng lúc có thể giúp họ thêm động lực duy trì việc cai thuốc lá.
Sau khi bỏ hút thuốc, chức năng phổi và thể lực có thể dần cải thiện, đồng thời giảm nguy cơ bệnh tim mạch và đột quỵ. Cai hút thuốc cũng giúp hạn chế người thân tiếp xúc với khói thuốc thụ động, nhất là trong không gian kín.

title: Grønlandske ledere mottatt som helter i Nuuk
content:
Grønlandske ledere mottatt som helter i Nuuk
En tydelig rørt regjeringssjef Jens-Frederik Nielsen og utenriksminister Múte B. Egede ble tatt imot av en stor menneskemengde på flyplassen i Nuuk onsdag.
Folkemengden viftet med grønlandske flagg og ropte Kalaallit Nunaat, som er det grønlandske navnet på Grønland, skriver landets kringkaster KNR.
– Grønland er grønlendernes land, sa parlamentsleder Kim Kielsen i sin hyllest til de to.
Danske medier, blant annet DR og TV 2 , merket seg at Nielsen og Egede var tydelig rørt av oppmerksomheten.
Nielsen undertegnet tirsdag en ny forsvars- og sikkerhetsavtale med USA og Danmark i New York. Den åpner for større amerikansk militær tilstedeværelse, men understreker også at denne retten skal brukes på en måte som respekterer grønlandsk samfunn og levesett. I tillegg må alle tre land bli enige om store avgjørelser på flere områder.
Fra flyplassen dro politikerne videre til et tradisjonelt kaffillerneq – bedre kjent som kaffemik på dansk – i kulturhuset i Nuuk. Her ble det også en rask pressekonferanse.
Her slo Nielsen fast at beboerne i Narsarsuaq ikke skal tvangsflyttes, skriver KNR.

title: Family shares hidden cost of cancer care
content:
Family shares hidden cost of cancer care
- Published
The parents of a teenage girl with a rare form of childhood cancer say the hidden costs of caring for their daughter have left them in fear of losing their home.
Maya, 13, from Hythe in Kent, was diagnosed with neuroblastoma at three years old, but relapsed in 2023 having been in remission for five years.
Her mother, Dellanie, said the pressure of paying a mortgage and bills whilst she and her husband, Terry, are working less to care for Maya is continuing to take its toll on their family of five.
Dellanie, an NHS nurse, said: "Whilst your child is poorly and you are fighting for her life, the bills don't stop coming."
She added: "My husband has lost his income as he is caring for Maya, and these days you need two people working just to keep your head above water.
"It has been very, very difficult but our aim has always been to to look after our child as well as each other.
"I always put a brave face on - of course I'm hurting, but I can't be in the corner crying."
Maya, who her mother described as a "larger than life person" who loves animals and music, was first diagnosed with neuroblastoma near her adrenal gland when she was three-years-old.
Neuroblastoma is a rare cancer which mainly affects children under five-years-old and around 100 children are diagnosed with it a year in the UK, according to Cancer Research UK.
After initially going into remission, Maya's neuroblastoma returned three years ago, and has since been cared for by specialist teams including at the Royal Marsden hospital in London, and Great Ormond Street Hospital.
In 2025, during a clinical trial of CAR T-cell therapy, a technique currently used to treat some types of leukaemia and lymphoma, Maya developed a brain injury which Dellanie said left her "profoundly disabled".
Her disability meant Terry had to leave his job to care for Maya full time, while Dellanie reduced her working hours to care for her, and support her husband.
Dellanie said: "I just have to be grateful for what we have got.
"At the moment, Maya is a fighter and there is so much fight in her."
'Thrown into chaos'
Charity Young Lives vs Cancer says families of children with cancer face average extra costs of around £700 a month, and an average loss of income of about £6,000 per household.
Sonia Malik, the charity's associate policy director, said: "We find people are having to dip into savings, and most of these costs are immediate.
"It impacts the whole family and their lives are thrown into chaos.
"The financial stress should be the last thing families have to think about."
Malik said that some support is available for cancer patients and their carers, such as financial support from charities, disability benefits and carer's allowance, but it can take time for families to receive benefits support.
